English.Char_Desc_2000:
Combine Document Files (called Combine Word Files up to version 1.0.1) joins Word (.docx, .doc) and Rich Text (.rtf) files into one, in the order you choose, with a line between each file. Press 1. Pick folder... to list every document in a folder in page-number order (page 2 before page 10), or Add files... to pick them one at a time. Each file has a tick box; files that can't be used (locked, damaged or empty) are greyed out with the reason. Move up, Move down, Move to top and Move to bottom set the order. Save the result as Word (.docx), older Word (.doc), Rich Text (.rtf) or PDF, then press 4. Combine. Each file keeps its own fonts, spacing, page size, orientation, margins, pictures, tables, lists, footnotes, endnotes and comments. Headers and footers come from the first file. You are asked before an existing combined file is replaced.
Before you install: Microsoft Word is optional: .docx files are combined and saved as .docx without it. Reading .doc and .rtf files, and saving as .doc, .rtf or PDF, need Word. Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit. The installer is not code-signed (a signing certificate is a paid yearly service), so Windows may show a blue "Windows protected your PC" box: click More info, then Run anyway. A few antivirus programs wrongly flag new unsigned programs; you can check the download against the SHA-256 fingerprint on its release page. No administrator password is needed.

Permissions.Distribution_Permissions: Combine Document Files is free to use and share. Download sites may list it and offer the unchanged Setup.exe, or link to the download page.
Permissions.EULA: Combine Document Files is free and comes with no warranty. Use it at your own risk. The free parts it is built from keep their own licenses, listed in the licenses folder it installs.
